name: Coriky
label: Dischord
lede: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina of the Evens took Joe Lally back from Rome, practiced for three years, and played their first show in a church without a name. Then a pandemic delayed the record.

eras.title: Lally moves home from Rome
eras.text: After Fugazi stopped, Joe Lally made solo records and raised a family in Rome. When he moved back to Washington in 2015, he started playing with Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina of The Evens, and the duo became a trio.

years.cap: The unnamed trio at St. Stephen & the Incarnation, Washington, November 11, 2018
years.src: Dischord: Coriky · Wikipedia: Coriky · Wikipedia: Joe Lally
years.h: Lally moves home and starts playing with MacKaye and Farina
years.p: Back in Washington, Joe Lally starts playing with Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina. It's the first time MacKaye and Lally share a band since Fugazi went on hiatus.
years.xp:
Lally and MacKaye started Fugazi together in 1987, and Lally played bass until the hiatus. In the gap he ran the Tolotta label through Dischord, played with [[John Frusciante|f1571db1-c672-4a54-a2cf-aaa329f26f0b]] in [[Ataxia|c2b5da4f-31c2-4a02-80a1-e00008378157]], and made three solo albums while living in Italy.

Dischord's Coriky bio is brief and a little dry: formed in 2015, no first show until 2018.

eras.title: Three years in, an open practice
eras.text: Nobody outside the room had heard the band. Its first public appearance came the way a lot of D.C. punk does: a benefit in a church, for a good cause, with the phones told to stay down.

years.cap: MacKaye, Farina and Lally at their first show, St. Stephen's church, Washington, November 11, 2018
years.h: An unnamed band plays St. Stephen's and calls it practice
years.p: Ian MacKaye, Amy Farina and Joe Lally raise money for the Loaves & Fishes meal program at St. Stephen's church in Washington. It's billed as an open practice, and MacKaye asks the crowd not to film.
years.xp:
Brooklyn Vegan assembled the night from fan posts. One attendee called it "a bit rough but good vibes. The Evens with a Fugazi groove." Another counted "sleepy kids & swell librarians" in the crowd on a Sunday night.

A third noted that MacKaye's stage banter was still on point.

eras.title: A debut that waits out the lockdown
eras.text: Coriky recorded the album the old Dischord way, with Don Zientara at Inner Ear. Two weeks before release day the country shut down, and the band picked the record stores over the calendar.

years.cap: Joe Lally on bass at the Georgetown Neighborhood Library, Washington, summer 2019
years.h: Inner Ear, Don Zientara, and the band at the boards too
years.p: Don Zientara, who has engineered decades of Dischord records, records the album at Inner Ear. MacKaye, Farina and Lally pitch in on engineering and mixing.

years.h: Kuriki, a dice game for touring bands, gives the trio its name
years.p: Ian MacKaye, Amy Farina and Joe Lally announce Coriky and put out Clean Kill, with a March 27 date for the debut album.
years.xp: Wikipedia traces the name to Kuriki, a dice game popular among touring bands. Clean Kill opens the album and runs 4:12.

years.cap: Ian MacKaye at the Georgetown Neighborhood Library, Washington, October 12, 2019
years.h: A free show at St. Stephen and the Incarnation, five weeks before release day
years.p: Coriky play for free at the Episcopal church in Washington on February 22, previewing an album due March 27.

q: As close to the much-missed Fugazi as it gets in 2020.
years.h: Coriky waits for the record stores to reopen
years.p: The debut was due March 27, 2020, until COVID-19 closed the shops. Dischord No. 190 came out digitally June 12 and on pink vinyl and CD June 26.
years.xp:
Rather than release it online while the stores that sell Dischord records were dark, the band and label held it back. Too Many Husbands followed in May as the second single.

Eleven songs in 37 minutes, from Clean Kill to Woulda Coulda. Metacritic scored it 84, Pitchfork gave it 7.8, and Stereogum made it album of the week, calling it "a triumphant record."

Kitty Empire gave it four stars in the Guardian. Laura Jane Grace picked it as her favorite album of 2020.

years.p: Mojo puts the album at 32 on its list of the year's 75 best. Metacritic ranks it fifth among 2020's best debuts.

sources.title: Brooklyn Vegan: Ian MacKaye, Joe Lally & Amy Farina's band played their first show
